gap: No result ChatGPT got says that EcoFlow STREAM, the only grid-feeding battery system ChatGPT showed a US price for, is limited by EcoFlow's own US page to sale and installation in Utah. The same page lists it as UL 1741 certified, not certified as a plug-in PV system, which is what SB 868 requires. That leaves a US shopper with off-grid battery kits that are priced today and range from $531 (ALLPOWERS P1800 + 200 W) to $1,499 (BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 2×200 W).
standout_why: I compared this against the three cited pages. californiabalconysolar.com/sb-868 gives the bill's requirements: 1,200 W per dwelling, certified as a plug-in PV system by UL or equivalent, and anti-backfeed. It names no products and no prices, and says nothing about batteries. pluginsolartracker.com/california also names no products, prices or batteries. KQED gives a $300–$2,200 range for kits that have no battery. It says products on the market 'do not yet meet the outlined requirements', but it names none. None of the three says which battery products a US shopper can buy, what they cost today, or that ChatGPT's top card (EcoFlow STREAM) is sold for Utah only.
decides: This moves the pick away from ChatGPT's lead card. A shopper outside Utah, including in California before or after Jan 1, 2027, cannot buy EcoFlow STREAM for plug-and-play use according to EcoFlow's US page. The STREAM page lists UL 1741, not a plug-in PV system certification. Anker's Solarbank 3 was described by ChatGPT itself as primarily a European product. So the practical US answer today is an off-grid power station plus panel, which runs devices from the battery's own outlets. In that group, the ALLPOWERS P1800 + 400 W kit (1,024 Wh, $698) is the cheapest 1 kWh-class battery-plus-400 W option I priced at a maker store. The BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 200 W kit ($1,199, 2,073.6 Wh) is the 2 kWh option. Both are kits we already list.
